grandparents_cupboard.reason: Rhubarb, apples, flour, butter, oats, sugar, almonds and spices are all plain kitchen staples.

supermarket.reason: Every ingredient is an everyday item at Tesco, and rhubarb is in mainstream supermarkets in late March.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a baking dish, a mixing bowl and the rubbing-in method, which a confident beginner can manage.

works.reason: The amounts suit a crumble for four, and 30 to 35 minutes at 200°C will cook the rhubarb and colour the topping; the sweet topping balances the lightly sugared tart fruit.

honest_times.reason: Twenty minutes covers cutting the fruit, chopping the almonds and rubbing in the butter, and the 45 cook minutes match the bake plus the 10-minute cool.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and spice is used in the steps, the names match their ids, and nothing unlisted appears.

seasonal_feel.reason: A warm rhubarb crumble suits late March, and the rhubarb is clearly the point of the dish.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are clear, homely British English with no restaurant language or preaching.

hearty_healthy.reason: It is fruit-heavy with oats and almonds in the topping and moderate sugar, a crumble a family would happily make again.
